issues.description: Class name mismatch: the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares the class as 'Image24' (class Image24) while the header also declares constructors/destructor named 'Bitmap24' and the implementation file (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines methods for 'Bitmap24::...'. The solution repository uses 'Bitmap24' consistently. This inconsistent identifier in the template header (Image24 vs Bitmap24) will cause compilation/linking failures and confuses students which class name to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class identifier consistent. Update the template header to declare 'class Bitmap24' instead of 'class Image24' so the header's class name matches the constructor/destructor names and the implementation. Concretely: change the 'class Image24' line to 'class Bitmap24' and keep the existing constructor/destructor/method declarations as-is. Alternatively, if you prefer the name Image24, rename the implementation and solution artifacts to Image24 consistently, but prefer updating the header to Bitmap24 to match the implementation and solution.
